name: Biryani By Kilo - Lower Parel
description:
At Biryani By Kilo, our Handi biryani is slow Dum-cooked using the choicest of ingredients, made fresh only on order. We deliver/serve Biryani in the same Handi in which it is Dum cooked on order to lock the delicious flavors, aromas & taste. BBK Kebabs, curries, breads & other Indian classical dishes are top notch too.
In today’s fast-paced world, we need to slow down and enjoy life’s precious moments, especially food. We believe that food must be relished with fursat, in every bite. So when you dig in to our food, it’s “Fursat Wala Yum, Dum Dumma Dum Dum”.'
We have 100+ outlets in 45+ cities and can be ordered through website, App, Call Centre (1800-212-2-212).

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve ordered from this place twice on Zomato since we are from Hyderabad and wanted to try their biryani. Both times, I ordered the Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani and the Lucknow Biryani.

Unfortunately, they didn’t follow the cooking instructions on either occasion, even though I mentioned that the order was specially prepared for us. I had clearly asked for it to be spicy 🌶️, but it wasn’t. I also requested cutlery both times—they missed it the first time, and again the second time. Since I’m staying in a hotel where they don’t provide Cutlery or serve food, it became very inconvenient to serve directly from the containers.

I also ordered Phirni. The first time, it tasted really good, so I ordered two portions the second time—but the taste was so bad that I had to throw them away.

Even the Salan (gravy) was inconsistent. The first time, it was tasty though a bit watery. This time I ordered two portions (one large and one small), and both were a disaster — very thin and lacking flavor.

Verdict : For price they are charging quantity they are providing is not worth any way. They are paying extra for pots and billing same to us with profit on everything they used.

featured_reviews.name: Avni Barai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Amidst all the chaos going around, this brand never fails to surprise me and my family! ☺️

Ordered lunch today from here… for me and my mom.

We ordered for Veg Biryani and Paneer 65.

Paneer 65 was so so delicious and so nicely cooked and perfectly served in a disposable and safe box. Also, paneer was so soft making it even more delicious!

And their veg biryani is like a piece of heaven on earth! They serve biryanis in an earthen pot with a chulhaa to heat that earthern pot. Chulhaa has candles inside it and then you have to keep that biryani filled earthen pot on a chulhaa for like 8-10 minutes and then you can open the lid and enjoy some delicious biryani. Filled with aroma of indian spices and cooked slowly in that pot and garnished with fried onions and giving it a proper shahi look! Loved it so much!! Biryani was served with onios, salan and raita. Amazingg!

We also ordered phirni. It was of saffron flavor and it was so yumm!

One can never go wrong with this place!

Must try! 😻😻

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
In these times of pandemic, we finally ordered for food and this time around we were keen to have Biryani. Had heard of Biryani By Kilo and we decided to give it a try. Packaging was superb, leak proof. Food came in quite warm. Talking about what all we ordered -

Kebab Platter which comes with 4 kebabs - Veg Galouti, Crispy Corn Stick, Kaju Ki Seekh and Paneer Multani. The packaging was quite neat. Of this Crispy Corn Stick was absolutely brilliant, must try. Also loved the Veg Galouti, wasn't dry at all. In fact quite quite soft and fresh, melts in mouth. Same was the case with Kaju Ki Seekh.

We had also called for Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, comes in 1/2 kg or 1 kg packs. It's packed in Handis. You also get another small handi with tealight candles which help keeping the biryani warm. This is quite unique, haven't seen this concept in any other delivery kitchens. Biryani is yum, I most definitely recommend it. Looking forward to trying Paneer Biryani next time.

We also called for Matka Phirni for dessert. Comes in a cute small Handi again. Phirni is brilliant, not too sweet just perfect. Quite thick as well. Superb food from Biryani By Kilo, wishing all the best!

Visited Ishaara at Palladium recently and it turned out to be a memorable dining experience—not just for the food, but for the overall concept and service.

The ambience is elegant yet calming, with a minimalistic design that allows you to relax and enjoy your meal without too much noise or distraction. It feels premium but still comfortable enough for a casual outing.

What really stands out is their unique service model, where the staff communicates through sign language. Despite that, the service is extremely smooth, attentive, and warm. You genuinely feel the effort and hospitality, which adds a special emotional value to the experience.

Coming to the food, we tried a variety of dishes:

* Nihari Soup – Deep, rich, and full of flavour. A great start to the meal, especially if you enjoy slow-cooked, meaty broths.
* Chicken Roll – Nicely done, with good balance of spices and texture. Simple but satisfying.

Overall, Ishaara is not just about dining—it’s about experiencing food with purpose. Great food, meaningful service, and a peaceful ambience make it worth visiting.

I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

Coming to the food... It was an absolute feast!

I had 4 pieces of Chicken Seekh Kebab. They were moist, flavourful and glazed with butter.

BBQ Chicken Pizza Square which blew my mind! The base was made out of Puff Pastry. The combination of Chicken, Cheese, Sauce and the Pastry went really well. But the chicken wasn’t smokey enough for my palate.

The mains,
Awadhi Chicken Biryani, the Lucknowi delight, I literally finished the last grain of rice. The balance between the Masala and the rice was perfect. The masala did have a spice kick from the Khara Masala and the fried onions. The large portion had 3 succulent pieces of Chicken and is enough for 2 people or one hefty eater. The raita helped cool down the heat from the Biryani.

Finally the dessert,
Salted Caramel Mousse, was a tad bit less on Caramel Taste as the Dark Chocolate overpowered the subtle Caramel. Not to forget it was an amazing dessert and pretty rich.

The whole meal was about ₹800 and it filled me and my friend. Would I recommend Charcoal eats; it’s definitely worth a try.

Our lunch at Punjab Grill, Phoenix Palladium Mall, turned out to be one of the most satisfying and comforting North Indian meals we’ve had in Mumbai. Being from North India, we always look for places that can recreate authentic flavours, and Punjab Grill once again lived up to expectations with its rich taste, warm ambience, and excellent service.

We ordered our all-time favourites — Dal Makhani and Paneer Lababdar, accompanied by Lachha Paranthas, Tandoori Rotis, and fresh salads. The Dal Makhani was slow-cooked to perfection, creamy, smoky, and just the right amount of buttery, reminding us of dhabas back home. The Paneer Lababdar was equally delicious: soft paneer cubes in a luscious, mildly spicy gravy that paired beautifully with the hot, crisp Lachha Paranthas. The Tandoori Rotis were perfectly roasted, light, and complemented the curries well. Every dish carried an unmistakable authentic North Indian aroma and taste.

The ambience of the restaurant added to the experience — elegant but cosy, with comfortable seating and warm lighting that made the meal feel unhurried and enjoyable. The environment was calm despite the mall rush, making it a great spot to relax after a movie.

What truly stood out was the courteous and attentive staff. They served promptly, checked in without being intrusive, and ensured every dish was fresh and hot. At the end of the meal, the liquid mouth freshener served in tiny tequila-style glasses was a delightful touch — refreshing, unique, and a fun way to conclude the lunch.

Overall, Punjab Grill offered a wonderful blend of flavour, comfort, and hospitality. For anyone craving authentic North Indian food in Mumbai, this place is always a dependable choice. A memorable lunch indeed!

Recently visited Banana Leaf Restaurant at Palladium, Phoenix Mall. The restaurant has a pleasant ambiance with comfortable seating and a clean, well-maintained dining area. What was particularly disappointing was that we had to repeatedly ask for basic necessities such as water, extra plates, cutlery, and other table requirements. These are things that should ideally be provided proactively, especially in a restaurant located in a premium destination like Palladium, Phoenix Mall.

The restaurant has great potential because the food is genuinely good and worth recommending. However, the dining experience was affected by the lack of attentiveness and the need to constantly remind the staff about simple requests. Better coordination among the service team and a more customer-focused approach would make a substantial difference.

Overall, Banana Leaf delivers excellent food with authentic flavors, making it a good choice for South Indian cuisine lovers. However, improvements in service speed and attention to detail are needed for the experience to match the quality of the food. I would visit again for the food, but I hope the service standards improve in the future.

featured_reviews.review_text:
During a recent visit to Yazu Pan Asian Supper Kitchen in Lower Parel, I had the opportunity to indulge in a diverse and flavorful spread that truly showcased the restaurant’s mastery over Asian cuisine. From the moment we arrived, the ambiance set the tone for a relaxed yet upscale dining experience. The service was courteous and efficient, with dishes arriving promptly and plated beautifully.

Our meal began with the Prawn Tempura Roll, which was light, crispy, and paired with just the right balance of sauces. It was followed by the Sriracha Chicken that packed a punch of heat, complemented by a slightly sweet undertone. The Yazu Signature Sichuan Garlic Prawn stood out with its bold flavors and perfectly cooked prawns, a definite must-try for seafood lovers. Another highlight was the Yazu Signature Chicken, which offered a rich and savory profile that paired well with the other mains.

For noodles, the Phad Thai Noodles were enjoyable, with a classic tamarind flavor and the right mix of textures. The Chicken in Hot Garlic Sauce added a spicy, garlicky depth to the meal that was satisfying and comforting. We also tried the Shojo, which added a refreshing and slightly lighter touch to the otherwise intense flavor profile of the dishes.

To end on a sweet note, we ordered the Mathilda Cakes Pull Me Up. It was a delightful dessert that offered a decadent and fun experience, perfectly capping off our evening.

Overall, Yazu delivered a memorable culinary experience with a well-rounded menu and elegant atmosphere. It's a great choice for those looking to explore Pan Asian cuisine with a modern twist in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazu is a Pan‑Asian “supper club” concept that brings together flavors from Japan, China, Thailand, Korea and Southeast Asia under one roof. The Lower Parel outlet is positioned as a flagship. The place is spacious combining indoor and outdoor elements. The branding emphasizes “visual experiences” — sculptural ceiling installations, patterned concrete flooring, carved wooden walls, lighting as focal décor elements. Ambience is amazing: stylish, atmospheric, good for evenings, date nights, or a premium outing. The décor and lighting get special and the ceiling installation, carved walls, and an aesthetic that’s “Instagram‑worthy.” After sundown, it transforms into a high‑energy bar/music venue  like “Studio Nights”.
Wide and ambitious menu: sushi, sashimi, maki, dim sum, baos (Taiwanese street bun), Teppanyaki, Robata grill items, curries, fusion dishes (e.g. “Asian Pizza‑San”) etc. They offer special dietary menus: Jain and Keto options. Go for signature dishes (e.g. sushi rolls, baos, dim sum) early; save room for dessert.
Top Picks:
• Black crispy Asparagus Roll (sushi) • Steamed Veg. Cheung Fung • Veg. Dimsum Experience Basket (7 piece) • Spicy Lotus root • Mah Poh Tofu etc.
• For soups: the Tom Kha, Tom Yum are superb.
• Desserts are also a highlight: “Pull Me Up Tiramisu”, “Berry Blossom Cheesecake”, “Salted Caramel Tart”, Coconut Panna Cotta etc. Presentation is premium, textures and flavors seem well balanced in many reviews.
• Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience. Loved its Samurai (cocktail), Shojo and Yashi (mocktails) which were flavorful and refreshing.
Attentive and polite staff who guide through the menu, make recommendations, and ensure a comfortable dining experience. Yazu Lower Parel is a strong pick if you're looking for a premium Pan‑Asian dining + bar experience in Mumbai. The ambience, décor, and overall concept are standout features. The place has a premium, elegant vibe and delivers a memorable night out.

featured_reviews.name: VlogWithFurkan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited SpiceKlub to explore their newly launched menu, and it was truly an impressive experience for anyone who enjoys modern Indian fusion cuisine.
We started with their appetizers, and the Masala Pav Bagel Bites were an absolute highlight. It’s a creative take on Mumbai’s classic masala pav, served inside sesame bagels with a perfect balance of spiced onion-tomato masala, buttery chutney, and cream cheese. The flavours felt familiar yet completely elevated.
The Desi Hummus Dip was another standout dish. Unlike regular hummus, this one blends creamy chickpea hummus with bold, smoky Pindi chole flavours. The crunchy toppings and spiced oil drizzle added great texture and depth, making it a must-try for fusion lovers.
For beverages, we tried the Jamun Sour and Kanji Martini. The Jamun Sour was refreshing, tangy, and well-balanced with a hint of citrus, while the Kanji Martini offered a unique fermented flavour with mustard and kala namak notes — definitely something different and worth experiencing.
In the main course, the Hyderabadi Chilli Roast was beautifully executed. Stuffed green chillies filled with herbed goat cheese paired perfectly with the rich peanut, sesame, and coconut-based salan, offering a great balance of spice and creaminess.
The most unique part of the experience was the Bubbling Kulfi. It’s served at an extreme temperature and cannot be eaten directly, making it an interactive dessert where you mix it with add-ons before enjoying. A fun and innovative concept that stands out.
Overall, SpiceKlub truly delivers when it comes to creativity, presentation, and flavour. It’s the perfect place for anyone looking to try something different from the usual dining options in Mumbai. Highly recommended for fusion food lovers!
